Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 53, verses 1–18:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} Allah swears by the star when it sets (hawa), i.e., when it falls below the horizon at the end of the night, as the night recedes and the day approaches, because in that there are great signs that warranted His swearing by it. The correct view is that "the star" (al-najm) is a generic noun encompassing all the stars. He swore by the stars to affirm the truth of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought of divine revelation, because there is a wondrous correspondence in this: Allah made the stars an adornment of the sky, and likewise revelation and its effects are an adornment of the earth. Were it not for the knowledge inherited from the prophets, people would be in a darkness far more intense than the darkness of the pitch-black night.

{2} What is sworn to is the absolution of the Messenger (ﷺ) from error in his knowledge and deviation in his intention, and from this it follows that he is guided in his knowledge, upright in his intention, and sincere in counsel to creation, unlike the people of error, who have corrupt knowledge and bad intention. Allah said, "your companion" (sahibukum), to remind them of what they know of him in terms of truthfulness and guidance, and that his affair is not hidden from them.

{3–4} "Nor does he speak from desire" means that his speech does not proceed from his own whim. "It is not but a revelation revealed" means that he follows only what is revealed to him of guidance and piety, in himself and in others. This indicates that the Sunnah is revelation from Allah to His Messenger (ﷺ), as Allah said: "And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom." It also indicates that he is protected from error in what he reports about Allah and His law, because his speech does not come from desire but from revelation that is revealed.

{5} Then He mentioned the teacher of the Messenger (ﷺ), who is Gabriel (peace be upon him), the most excellent, strongest and most perfect of the noble angels, saying: "Taught him one mighty in power." That is, Gabriel, mighty in power, descended with the revelation to the Messenger (ﷺ); that is, one of great outward and inward strength, capable of carrying out what Allah commanded him to carry out, and capable of conveying the revelation to the Messenger (ﷺ) and preventing the devils from snatching it or inserting into it what is not part of it. This is among Allah's preservation of His revelation: that He sent it with this strong, trustworthy messenger.

{6} "Possessor of strength" means possessor of power, good character, and outward and inward beauty. "And he stood firm" refers to Gabriel (peace be upon him).

{7} "While he was on the highest horizon" means the horizon of the sky, which is higher than the earth. He is of the exalted spirits, which the devils cannot reach and cannot gain access to.

{8} "Then he drew near": Gabriel drew near to the Prophet (ﷺ) to convey the revelation to him, "and came down" to him from the highest horizon.

{9} "And was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer": in his nearness to him, that is, the measure of two bows, and the bow is well known, "or nearer," that is, closer than two bows. This indicates the complete directness of his contact with the Messenger (ﷺ) in conveying the message, and that there was no intermediary between him and Gabriel (peace be upon him).

{10} "So He revealed" by means of Gabriel (peace be upon him) "to His servant [Muhammad (ﷺ)] what He revealed," that is, what He revealed to him of the great law and the upright news.

{11–12} "The heart did not falsify what it saw": that is, the heart and sight of the Messenger (ﷺ) agreed with the revelation that Allah revealed to him, and his hearing, sight and heart were in harmony upon it. This is evidence of the perfection of the revelation Allah revealed to him, and that he received it from Him in a manner about which there is no doubt, no ambiguity, and no uncertainty. So his heart did not deny what his eyes saw, and he did not doubt it.
It is possible that what is meant is what he (ﷺ) saw on the night of the Isra' of the great signs of Allah, and that he was certain of it as truth with his heart and vision; this is the correct interpretation of the noble verse. It has been said that what is meant is the Messenger's (ﷺ) seeing of his Lord on the night of the Isra' and His speaking to him. This is the choice of many scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, who thereby affirm that the Messenger (ﷺ) saw his Lord in this world.
However, the correct view is the first, and that what is meant is Gabriel (peace be upon him), as the context indicates, and that Muhammad (ﷺ) saw Gabriel in his original form, which he has, twice: once on the highest horizon beneath the lowest heaven, as previously mentioned, and the second time above the seventh heaven on the night the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Isra'.

{13–14} Hence He said: "And he certainly saw him in another descent," that is, Muhammad saw Gabriel another time descending to him, "at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary," which is a very great tree above the seventh heaven. It was named the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary because whatever ascends from the earth ends at it, and whatever descends from Allah, such as revelation and other things, descends to it; or because the knowledge of created beings ends at it, that is, because it is above the heavens and the earth, so it is the boundary of their knowledge; or for other reasons. And Allah knows best. So Muhammad (ﷺ) saw Gabriel in that place, which is the abode of the pure, beautiful, exalted spirits, which no devil or other wicked spirit approaches.

{15} Near that tree is "the Garden of Refuge," that is, the Garden that gathers every bliss, such that it is a place where all wishes end, desires long for it, and longings take refuge in it. This is evidence that the Garden is in the highest places and above the seventh heaven.

{16} "When there covered the Lote-tree that which covered": that is, there covered it a great matter from the command of Allah, whose description no one knows except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

{17} "His sight did not swerve," that is, it did not turn right or left from its object, "nor did it transgress," that is, the sight did not go beyond its limit. This is the perfection of his courtesy (ﷺ), that he stood in the station Allah established for him, and did not fall short of it, nor exceed it, nor deviate from it. This is the most complete form of great courtesy, in which he surpassed the first and the last. Failure occurs in one of these matters: either the servant does not perform what he is commanded, or performs it with negligence, or with excess, or with deviation to the right or left. All of these are negated from him (ﷺ).

{18} "He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Lord": of the Garden and the Fire and other matters which he (ﷺ) saw on the night he was taken on the Isra'.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 53, verse 26:

{26} Allah the Exalted says, rebuking those who worship others besides Him, among the angels and others, and who claim that they will benefit them and intercede for them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing﴾ — from among the angels brought near and the noble angels — ﴿except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾; that is, it will not benefit anyone who calls upon them, clings to them, and hopes in them. ﴿Except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾; that is, both conditions must be met together: His permission for the intercession, and His approval of the one for whom intercession is made. It is well known and established that Allah accepts from deeds only that which is sincerely for the sake of Allah's Face and in which the doer conforms to the Shari'ah. Thus the polytheists have no share in the intercession of the intercessors, and [indeed] they have cut themselves off from the mercy of the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.

{27} That is: the polytheists, who deny His messengers and do not believe in the Hereafter, because of their disbelief in the Hereafter, have become bold in the sayings and actions they have dared to commit, which oppose Allah and His Messenger. Among them is their saying: "The angels are daughters of Allah!" They did not exalt their Lord above having offspring, nor did they honor the angels and hold them in reverence by calling them females. Yet they have no knowledge of this, neither from Allah nor from His Messenger, nor do the natural disposition (fitrah) and the intellects indicate it. Rather, all knowledge points to the opposite of their claim, and that Allah is far above having children or a consort, for He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. And the angels are honored, brought near to Allah, and busy in His service: {they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded}.

{28} The polytheists only follow in this ugly saying mere conjecture (zann), which does not avail against the truth at all, for the truth must be grounded in certainty (yaqin) derived from conclusive proofs (adillah qati'ah) and clear demonstrations (baraheen sati'ah).

{29} Since this has been the habit of those mentioned, that they have no aim in following the truth, and their only aim and purpose is what their souls desire, Allah commanded His Messenger to turn away from those who turn their backs on His remembrance, which is the Wise Reminder, the Great Qur'an, [and the Noble News]. So he turned away from beneficial knowledge and sought nothing but the life of this world; this is the limit of their intention. It is well known that a servant works only for the thing he desires, so the striving of these people is confined to this world and its pleasures and desires; however they obtain them, and by whatever means they present themselves, they hasten to seize them.

{30} {That is the extent of their knowledge}; that is, this is the limit and furthest reach of their knowledge. As for those who believe in the Hereafter and affirm it, the people of understanding and intellect, their concern and aspiration is for the Abode of the Hereafter, and their knowledge is the best and most exalted of knowledge, namely the knowledge taken from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ). Allah the Exalted knows best who deserves guidance, so He guides him, and who does not deserve it, so He leaves him to himself and forsakes him, and he strays from the path of Allah. For this reason He said, the Exalted: {Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path, and He knows best who is guided}: He places His favor where He knows the fitting place for it.

He disposes of them with the disposal of a mighty king over his servants and slaves: He executes His decree upon them, applies His legislation (shar') to them, commands and forbids them, and recompenses them for what He commanded and forbade, rewarding the obedient and punishing the disobedient. ﴿That He may recompense those who did evil﴾ with deeds of evil, from the evils of disbelief and what is less than it of acts of disobedience, and for what they did of deeds of wrongdoing, with a dreadful punishment; ﴿and recompense those who did good﴾ in the worship of God, and who did good to the creatures of God with various kinds of benefit, ﴿with the best﴾; that is, with a good state in this world and the Hereafter. The greatest and most sublime of that is the good pleasure of their Lord and the attainment of Paradise and the bliss within it.

{32} Then He mentioned their attributes, saying: ﴿Those who avoid major sins and immoralities﴾; that is, they do what God has commanded them of obligatory duties, the abandonment of which would be among the major sins, and they abstain from the great prohibitions, such as fornication, drinking wine, consuming usury (riba), murder, and similar grave sins. ﴿Except for minor offenses﴾ (al-lamam): these are the small sins which their doer does not persist in, or which the servant commits once after another, occasionally and rarely. Mere commission of these does not exclude the servant from being among the good-doers, for these, together with performing the obligatory duties and avoiding the prohibitions, fall under the forgiveness of God, which encompasses all things. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾. This weakness exists and is witnessed in you since God brought you forth from the earth, and when you were in the wombs of your mothers, and it has never ceased to exist in you, although God has indeed placed in you a strength for what He commanded you. But weakness has not ceased; so, because of His knowledge of these your conditions, divine wisdom and the lordly generosity require that He enfold you with His mercy, forgiveness and pardon, overwhelm you with His kindness, and remove from you crimes and sins. This is especially so when the servant's aim is the good pleasure of his Lord at all times, his striving is directed toward what brings him near to Him in most moments, and he flees from the sins for which he is detested by his Master, yet a slip occurs from him after another slip. For God, may He be exalted, is the most generous of the generous and the most bounteous of the bounteous, more merciful to His servants than a mother to her child. Thus, for such a person, it is inevitable that forgiveness from his Lord is near, and that God will be responsive to him in all his states. As for people, they cannot avail you anything against God.

As for people, they cannot avail you anything against God.

{33–35} God Most High says: Have you considered how ugly the state of one who was commanded to worship his Lord and to affirm His oneness, yet turned away and refused? If his soul allows him to give a little, he does not keep it up. Rather, he is stingy, withholds, and refuses. Goodness is not his natural disposition or character. His nature is to turn away from obedience and to not persist in doing good. Despite this, he praises himself and places himself in a rank other than the one God has assigned him.

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees it?﴾ Does he know the unseen so that he reports it? Or is he one who attributes falsehood to God and presumes against Him, combining two forbidden things, wrongdoing and self-praise? This is indeed the reality, since it is known that he has no knowledge of the unseen. And even if it were supposed that he claimed it, the decisive reports about the unseen that came through the infallible Prophet (ﷺ) contradict his claim, and this is proof of its falsehood.

{36–37} ﴿Or has he not been informed﴾ — this claimant — ﴿of what is in the scriptures of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled?﴾ That is, who carried out everything God tested him with and commanded him, from the laws and the fundamentals and branches of religion.

{38–41} In those scriptures there are many rulings, the most important of which is what God mentioned in His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾. That is, every doer has his good and bad deeds, and he has nothing from the deeds and striving of another, and no one bears another's sin. ﴿And that his striving will be seen﴾ — in the Hereafter — so that his good is distinguished from his evil. ﴿Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense﴾, that is, one who has completed all his deeds: the purely good is rewarded with the best, the purely evil with the worst, and the mixed according to its measure. It is a recompense by which all creation acknowledges His justice and goodness and praises God for it. Even the people of the Fire will enter the Fire while their hearts are full of praise for their Lord and acknowledgment of His perfect wisdom, and abhorrence of themselves, and that they are the ones who brought themselves to ruin and led themselves to the worst of destinations.

Some have used His saying [Exalted is He]: ﴿and that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾ as evidence by those who hold that acts of worship may not be gifted to the living or to the dead. They say: because God said ﴿that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾, so the reaching of another's striving to him contradicts that. There is room for scrutiny in this argument. The verse indicates only that man has nothing except what he himself strove for, and this is a truth on which there is no disagreement. Nothing in it indicates that he does not benefit from another's striving when that other gives it to him as a gift, just as a person has from wealth only what is in his possession and under his control, and yet this does not mean he cannot own what another has given him from his own property.

{42} And His saying: ﴿and that to your Lord is the final return﴾, that is, to Him all affairs end, and to Him things and creatures return through resurrection and rising. To God is the ultimate end in every state. To Him ends knowledge, judgment, mercy, and all other perfections.

{43} ﴿And that it is He who makes laugh and makes weep﴾, that is, He is the one who created the causes of laughter and weeping, and He is the one who [creates] good and evil, joy and happiness, worry and sorrow. He, glorified is He, has perfect wisdom in this.

{44} ﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾, that is, He alone brings into existence and annihilates. He who created creation and commanded and forbade them will return them after their death and will repay them for the deeds they did in the abode of this world.

{45–46} ﴿And that He created the pairs﴾: he explained them with His saying ﴿the male and the female﴾. This is a generic term including all animals, speaking and beasts alike. He alone created them ﴿from a drop when it is emitted﴾. This is among the greatest proofs of His complete power and His unique great might: He brought into existence those animals, small and large, from a weak drop of despised water, then nurtured it, perfected it until it reached what it reached. Then the human being becomes either one who attains the highest stations in the most exalted heights, or one who falls to the lowest states in the lowest depths.

{47} For this reason He used the beginning as proof of the return, saying: ﴿And that upon Him is the other creation﴾. He will return the servants from their graves, gather them for the appointed day, and recompense them for good and evil deeds.

{48} ﴿And that it is He who makes rich and grants possessions﴾, that is, He enriches the servants by facilitating the affairs of their livelihood through trade and various kinds of earnings from crafts and other means. ﴿And grants possessions﴾, that is, He grants His servants wealth of all kinds, by which they become owners and possessors of much property. This is among His blessings, that He informed them that all blessings come from Him, and this obliges the servants to thank Him and worship Him alone, with no partner.

{49} ﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾: this is the well-known star called al-Shi'ra al-'Abur, also called al-Mirzam. God singled it out for mention although He is the Lord of everything, because this star was among the things worshipped in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance). So God informed that what the polytheists worship is a created, managed, and governed thing. How, then, could it be taken as gods besides God?

{50} ﴿And that He destroyed the first 'Ad﴾: they were the people of Hud (peace be upon him), when they denied Hud, and God destroyed them with a furious, violent wind.

{51} ﴿And Thamud﴾: the people of Salih (peace be upon him). God sent him to Thamud, but they denied him. God sent to them the she-camel as a sign, but they hamstrung her and denied him, so God destroyed them. ﴿And He spared none﴾: He did not leave any of them, but annihilated them to the last one.

{52} ﴿And the people of Noah before, indeed they were the most unjust and most transgressive﴾ among these nations, so God destroyed and drowned them.

{53–54} ﴿And the overturned cities﴾: they were the people of Lot (peace be upon him). ﴿He hurled down﴾, that is, God struck them with a punishment with which He had punished no one among the worlds: He turned the lower part of their dwellings to the top, and rained upon them stones of baked clay. For this He said: ﴿so there covered them what covered﴾, that is, there came upon them of painful, grievous punishment what came upon them, a great thing that cannot be described.

{55} ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you dispute?﴾ That is: which of the blessings and bounties of God, O human, will you doubt? For God's blessings are manifest and admit no doubt in any way. No blessing is with the servants except from Him, and none averts afflictions except Him.

{56} ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾: that is, this Qurashi, Hashimi Messenger, Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, is no novelty among the messengers. Rather, messengers before him came and called to what he called to. So why do you deny his message? By what proof do you nullify his call? Is his character not the highest character of the noble messengers? Does he not call to every good and forbid every evil? Did he not bring the noble Qur'an, to which falsehood cannot come from before it or behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, Praiseworthy? Did God not destroy those who denied the messengers before him? So what prevents punishment from the deniers of Muhammad, the master of messengers, the leader of the righteous, and the guide of the radiant ones?

{57} ﴿The approaching one has drawn near﴾, that is, the Resurrection has drawn near, its time has approached, and its signs have appeared. ﴿There is none to remove it besides God﴾, that is, when the Resurrection comes and the promised punishment comes upon them.

{58} Then He threatened those who deny the message of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who reject the noble Qur'an he brought, saying:

{59} ﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse?﴾ That is: do you wonder at this discourse which is the best, most excellent, and most noble of speech, and do you regard it as one of the matters contrary to custom, extraordinary, and contrary to known realities? This comes from their ignorance, misguidance, and obstinacy. Otherwise, it is the discourse which, when it speaks, is truthful, and when it says a word, it is the decisive word, not a jest. It is the Great Qur'an, which, if it had been sent down upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart from fear of God. It increases those of understanding in opinion, intellect, firmness, steadfastness, certainty, and faith. Rather, it is those who wonder at it and deride it whose intellect deserves to be marveled at, and their folly and misguidance.

{60} ﴿And you laugh and do not weep﴾: that is, you hasten to laughter and mockery of it, though it is what should move souls, soften hearts, and make eyes weep, by hearing its commands and prohibitions, attending to its promise and warning, and attending to its true and good reports.

{61} ﴿While you are proud﴾, that is, heedless and distracted from it and from reflecting upon it. This is from the small measure of your intellects and your religion. If you had worshipped God and sought His pleasure in all circumstances, you would not be in this condition which people of intellect disdain.

{62} For this God Most High said: ﴿So prostrate to God and worship﴾. The command to prostrate to God specifically indicates its excellence and that it is the essence and core of worship, for its spirit is humility before God and submission to Him. Prostration is the greatest state in which the servant submits, for he submits his heart and body and places the noblest of his limbs upon the humble earth, the place of treading by feet. Then He commanded worship in general, encompassing all that God loves and is pleased with of deeds and sayings, outward and inward.

This is indeed the reality, since it is known that he has no knowledge of the unseen. And even if it were supposed that he claimed it, the decisive reports about the unseen that came through the infallible Prophet (ﷺ) contradict his claim, and this is proof of its falsehood.

{36–37} ﴿Or has he not been informed﴾ — this claimant — ﴿of what is in the scriptures of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled?﴾ That is, who carried out everything God tested him with and commanded him, from the laws and the fundamentals and branches of religion.

{38–41} In those scriptures there are many rulings, the most important of which is what God mentioned in His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾. That is, every doer has his good and bad deeds, and he has nothing from the deeds and striving of another, and no one bears another's sin. ﴿And that his striving will be seen﴾ — in the Hereafter — so that his good is distinguished from his evil. ﴿Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense﴾, that is, one who has completed all his deeds: the purely good is rewarded with the best, the purely evil with the worst, and the mixed according to its measure. It is a recompense by which all creation acknowledges His justice and goodness and praises God for it. Even the people of the Fire will enter the Fire while their hearts are full of praise for their Lord and acknowledgment of His perfect wisdom, and abhorrence of themselves, and that they are the ones who brought themselves to ruin and led themselves to the worst of destinations.

Some have used His saying [Exalted is He]: ﴿and that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾ as evidence by those who hold that acts of worship may not be gifted to the living or to the dead. They say: because God said ﴿that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾, so the reaching of another's striving to him contradicts that. There is room for scrutiny in this argument. The verse indicates only that man has nothing except what he himself strove for, and this is a truth on which there is no disagreement. Nothing in it indicates that he does not benefit from another's striving when that other gives it to him as a gift, just as a person has from wealth only what is in his possession and under his control, and yet this does not mean he cannot own what another has given him from his own property.

{42} And His saying: ﴿and that to your Lord is the final return﴾, that is, to Him all affairs end, and to Him things and creatures return through resurrection and rising. To God is the ultimate end in every state. To Him ends knowledge, judgment, mercy, and all other perfections.

{43} ﴿And that it is He who makes laugh and makes weep﴾, that is, He is the one who created the causes of laughter and weeping, and He is the one who [creates] good and evil, joy and happiness, worry and sorrow. He, glorified is He, has perfect wisdom in this.

{44} ﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾, that is, He alone brings into existence and annihilates. He who created creation and commanded and forbade them will return them after their death and will repay them for the deeds they did in the abode of this world.

{45–46} ﴿And that He created the pairs﴾: he explained them with His saying ﴿the male and the female﴾. This is a generic term including all animals, speaking and beasts alike. He alone created them ﴿from a drop when it is emitted﴾. This is among the greatest proofs of His complete power and His unique great might: He brought into existence those animals, small and large, from a weak drop of despised water, then nurtured it, perfected it until it reached what it reached. Then the human being becomes either one who attains the highest stations in the most exalted heights, or one who falls to the lowest states in the lowest depths.

{47} For this reason He used the beginning as proof of the return, saying: ﴿And that upon Him is the other creation﴾. He will return the servants from their graves, gather them for the appointed day, and recompense them for good and evil deeds.

{48} ﴿And that it is He who makes rich and grants possessions﴾, that is, He enriches the servants by facilitating the affairs of their livelihood through trade and various kinds of earnings from crafts and other means. ﴿And grants possessions﴾, that is, He grants His servants wealth of all kinds, by which they become owners and possessors of much property. This is among His blessings, that He informed them that all blessings come from Him, and this obliges the servants to thank Him and worship Him alone, with no partner.

{49} ﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾: this is the well-known star called al-Shi'ra al-'Abur, also called al-Mirzam. God singled it out for mention although He is the Lord of everything, because this star was among the things worshipped in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance). So God informed that what the polytheists worship is a created, managed, and governed thing. How, then, could it be taken as gods besides God?

{50} ﴿And that He destroyed the first 'Ad﴾: they were the people of Hud (peace be upon him), when they denied Hud, and God destroyed them with a furious, violent wind.

{51} ﴿And Thamud﴾: the people of Salih (peace be upon him). God sent him to Thamud, but they denied him. God sent to them the she-camel as a sign, but they hamstrung her and denied him, so God destroyed them. ﴿And He spared none﴾: He did not leave any of them, but annihilated them to the last one.

{52} ﴿And the people of Noah before, indeed they were the most unjust and most transgressive﴾ among these nations, so God destroyed and drowned them.

{53–54} ﴿And the overturned cities﴾: they were the people of Lot (peace be upon him). ﴿He hurled down﴾, that is, God struck them with a punishment with which He had punished no one among the worlds: He turned the lower part of their dwellings to the top, and rained upon them stones of baked clay. For this He said: ﴿so there covered them what covered﴾, that is, there came upon them of painful, grievous punishment what came upon them, a great thing that cannot be described.

{55} ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you dispute?﴾ That is: which of the blessings and bounties of God, O human, will you doubt? For God's blessings are manifest and admit no doubt in any way. No blessing is with the servants except from Him, and none averts afflictions except Him.

{56} ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾: that is, this Qurashi, Hashimi Messenger, Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, is no novelty among the messengers. Rather, messengers before him came and called to what he called to. So why do you deny his message? By what proof do you nullify his call? Is his character not the highest character of the noble messengers? Does he not call to every good and forbid every evil? Did he not bring the noble Qur'an, to which falsehood cannot come from before it or behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, Praiseworthy? Did God not destroy those who denied the messengers before him? So what prevents punishment from the deniers of Muhammad, the master of messengers, the leader of the righteous, and the guide of the radiant ones?

{57} ﴿The approaching one has drawn near﴾, that is, the Resurrection has drawn near, its time has approached, and its signs have appeared. ﴿There is none to remove it besides God﴾, that is, when the Resurrection comes and the promised punishment comes upon them.

{58} Then He threatened those who deny the message of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who reject the noble Qur'an he brought, saying:

{59} ﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse?﴾ That is: do you wonder at this discourse which is the best, most excellent, and most noble of speech, and do you regard it as one of the matters contrary to custom, extraordinary, and contrary to known realities? This comes from their ignorance, misguidance, and obstinacy. Otherwise, it is the discourse which, when it speaks, is truthful, and when it says a word, it is the decisive word, not a jest. It is the Great Qur'an, which, if it had been sent down upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart from fear of God. It increases those of understanding in opinion, intellect, firmness, steadfastness, certainty, and faith. Rather, it is those who wonder at it and deride it whose intellect deserves to be marveled at, and their folly and misguidance.

{60} ﴿And you laugh and do not weep﴾: that is, you hasten to laughter and mockery of it, though it is what should move souls, soften hearts, and make eyes weep, by hearing its commands and prohibitions, attending to its promise and warning, and attending to its true and good reports.

{61} ﴿While you are proud﴾, that is, heedless and distracted from it and from reflecting upon it. This is from the small measure of your intellects and your religion. If you had worshipped God and sought His pleasure in all circumstances, you would not be in this condition which people of intellect disdain.

{62} For this God Most High said: ﴿So prostrate to God and worship﴾. The command to prostrate to God specifically indicates its excellence and that it is the essence and core of worship, for its spirit is humility before God and submission to Him. Prostration is the greatest state in which the servant submits, for he submits his heart and body and places the noblest of his limbs upon the humble earth, the place of treading by feet. Then He commanded worship in general, encompassing all that God loves and is pleased with of deeds and sayings, outward and inward.

The end of the commentary on Surat an-Najm.
And praise be to God, whose praise we cannot count; rather He is as He praised Himself and beyond what His servants praise Him, and may God bless Muhammad and grant him abundant peace.
